target.title: fix: expose replayed chat.send errors to retrying clients
target.body:
Closes #103703

Related: #98203
Supersedes: #98206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where backend clients retrying a failed `chat.send` with the same idempotency key could not tell that the Gateway had returned a stored result. A cached retryable error therefore looked fresh and could be resubmitted until the client's retry budget was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the broad metadata forwarding proposed in #98206 with a narrow negotiated contract:

- `response-replay` is an explicit client capability.
- The only wire metadata is the closed JSON shape `{ replayed: true }`.
- `RespondFn` keeps arbitrary diagnostic metadata in a separate log-only argument.
- Clients without the capability receive the unchanged strict response envelope.
- The official TypeScript Gateway client advertises the capability and exposes `GatewayClientRequestError.replayed`, providing an in-tree consumer.

`runId`, diagnostic `error`/`channel` values, and plugin metadata are never copied into the response metadata object.

## User Impact

Retrying clients can stop resubmitting the same idempotency key after the Gateway returns a stored retryable error. Existing clients and native apps that do not advertise `response-replay` see no new response-frame fields.

## Evidence

- Post-rebase focused run: 67 unit tests and 110 Gateway tests passed.
- Full TypeScript project graph passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json`.
- Full build passed with the repository's no-pnpm fallback: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs`.
- Formatting passed for every changed TypeScript/Markdown file.
- Extensions and scripts lint shards passed; the changed Gateway responder passed targeted type-aware core lint.
- Protocol and Swift models were regenerated; `ResponseFrame.meta` remains optional with a default-`nil` Swift initializer parameter.
- Tests verify the strict schema rejects arbitrary/legacy metadata, legacy clients receive no `meta`, opted-in clients receive only `{ replayed: true }`, cached `chat.send` paths supply the dedicated wire argument, and the TypeScript client consumes it on request errors.

The live WebSocket capture in #98206 already established that the original responder path dropped metadata. This PR does not repeat that transport-only proof; it adds the consumer, negotiation, safety boundary, and client-consumption proof requested in the closing review.
